projects.title: psow
projects.description: Technical research experiment evaluating the ergonomics, migration cost, and safety guarantees of two modern stacks — C++20 with Eigen and Rust — for porting a legacy C++/MFC finite element kernel. The scope is deliberately narrow: a single 15-node quadratic triangular prism (PSOW) element, with shape function formulas transcribed verbatim from the original reference implementation (math preserved bit-for-bit). The experiment is not production code; the repository serves as a working scratchpad for engineering notes and comparative observations prior to a full FEM kernel migration decision. Both ports are covered by an identical verification suite: partition of unity checks, Kronecker delta property at nodes, Jacobian non-singularity across the reference element, and derivative cross-validation against finite-difference approximations. The original computational code was authored by a third party and is used here as a reference with the author's consent; licensing of this repository and any further publication remain subject to separate agreement with the original author.

projects.title: t1dwh
projects.description: Academic prototype (2024 – early 2025) exploring distributed Data Warehouse (DWH) architectural patterns on Greenplum (MPP, PostgreSQL-based) with Apache Airflow for deterministic ETL orchestration. The project formalizes evaluation of DWH topologies (Kimball 1-2NF vs Inmon 3NF vs Data Vault) and executes a Kimball-derived dimensional model optimized for OLAP query patterns. Core engineering deliverables include a multi-tiered data architecture (Staging, DDS, Data Marts), implementation of Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Type 2) via hash-based change detection (MD5) for temporal data consistency, and storage engine optimization via columnar orientation, ZSTD/RLE compression algorithms, and range partitioning. The ETL subsystem utilizes postgres_fdw for federated data ingestion, Airflow DAGs with XCom for stateful inter-task coordination, and PL/pgSQL functions for incremental loading with high-water mark semantics. The prototype enforces idempotency, rigorous exception handling with quarantine patterns, and transaction isolation analysis (Repeatable Read, Serializable) for data consistency guarantees.
